author: Pavan Kumar
objective: Measure whether Gemini models mention and recommend Firebolt when developers ask realistic analytics database selection questions.
method_summary: Run a fixed set of developer-style prompts across a small group of Gemini models. For each answer, check whether Firebolt is mentioned, where it ranks among the products named, and whether it is recommended as a fit for the stated workload. Mention and rank are decided by deterministic text checks. An LLM judge is used only to explain the answer, not to detect mentions.

models.role: Fast baseline model with the highest daily quota in this account. Also used as the judge model.
Stronger Flash model, used to check whether better reasoning changes how often Firebolt appears.

prompt_categories.direct_comparison: Tests whether the model can compare Firebolt against a named competitor.
prompt_categories.workload_discovery: Tests whether Firebolt appears when the user describes the workload but does not name Firebolt.
prompt_categories.lakehouse_iceberg: Tests Firebolt positioning around S3, Parquet, Iceberg, and external table analytics.
prompt_categories.migration: Tests whether Firebolt is suggested when a team has pain with its current system.
prompt_categories.negative_tradeoff: Tests whether the model understands when Firebolt is not the right fit.
prompt_categories.category_discovery: Tests whether Firebolt appears naturally in a broad category question.

limitations: This is a small diagnostic benchmark, not a full market study.
Only Gemini models are included in this run.
The run uses 8 prompts per model to stay inside the free Gemini quota.
Model answers can change over time as model versions and training data change.
The judge model writes the explanation text, so important rows should still be read by a person.
The result is most useful when the same prompt set is rerun after public content about Firebolt changes.
